newsitem.title: USA: Greens cry foul on World Bank's Chile dam report.
newsitem.headline: Greens cry foul on World Bank's Chile dam report.

text.p: An environmental group Thursday accused the World Bank of trying to suppress a critical report on the Pangue Dam project in Chile.

The independent study on Pangue and a much bigger hydroelectric dam, Ralco, found that Chilean electricity giant Endesa had failed to meet some of the environmental and social conditions of a $150 million loan from the World Bank's private sector arm, the International Finance Corp.
As a result, Endesa earlier this year paid back the loan and turned to a German bank for financing.
Environmentalists want to see the whole report because Chile is about to make a decision on whether to license the massive Ralco dam, which green groups say should not go ahead.
"That report says whether the Bank's been snowed on this," said Andrea Durbin, director of international projects for Friends of the Earth.
Friends of the Earth said that, in a June 2 letter, World Bank President James Wolfensohn reneged on a promise to release the report.

Endesa "considers a number of statements made in the report to be erroneous and defamatory...and that other statements in the report disclose information which, in the view of Pangue management, IFC is legally bound to keep confidential," Wolfensohn said in the letter to the group.

IFC spokesman Mark Constantine said the bank was in a difficult position trying to balance its public obligation to be as transparent as possible while at the same time working with private sector clients who expect to keep their business confidential.

Wolfensohn told the group that the IFC and Pangue had recently signed an agreement to ensure the company addressed environmental and social problems raised in the report. But Durbin said the World Bank was refusing to release the terms of the agreement.
"At the moment that remains a confidential document at the company's request," Constantine said.
